gamma_events.title: Highest temperature in Munich on August 4?
gamma_events.description:
This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Munich Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 4 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Munich Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/de/munich/EDDM.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

Current ensemble runs show daytime maxima reaching the mid-30s Celsius under mostly sunny conditions and light winds, with limited cloud cover or precipitation expected to suppress peaks. This aligns with observed regional heat trends through early August, where official measurements have already approached similar thresholds. Model spread remains modest but acknowledges typical uncertainties in boundary-layer heating and local urban effects that could shift the exact maximum by 1–2°C. Updated runs ahead of resolution will refine these implied probabilities as new observational data arrives.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Trader sentiment for London's highest temperature on August 4, 2026, centers on 28–30°C as the dominant range, with 29°C holding the highest implied probability at 48.5%.** This positioning reflects ensemble forecast guidance from the Met Office and ECMWF, which indicate a continuation of above-average warmth driven by southerly flow of subtropical air and residual high-pressure influence across southern England. August climatology places London's typical daily maximum near 22–23°C, so current model consensus represents a +6–7°C anomaly consistent with the broader 2026 summer pattern of repeated heat episodes.

Urban heat-island effects in central London stations, combined with light winds and partial cloud cover, support peak readings in this band. Recent model runs have shown limited spread, keeping 31°C+ probabilities low while assigning minimal weight to 27°C or below. As the day progresses, real-time observations from Heathrow, Kew, and Northolt—updated hourly by the Met Office—will determine the exact maximum and drive any final repricing before resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Trader sentiment for Tokyo's highest temperature on August 5 centers on a narrow band around 30–31°C, driven by the latest Japan Meteorological Agency (JMA) forecast for mostly cloudy skies with scattered showers possible later in the day.** This setup typically limits daytime heating compared to clear, stable summer conditions, keeping the daily maximum near or slightly below seasonal norms despite the broader expectation of above-average temperatures for August 2026.

The Pacific High remains influential, sustaining warm, humid air masses across Honshu, yet the immediate synoptic pattern favors increased cloud cover and moisture that caps peak readings. Official guidance points to a high near 29–32°C, aligning with historical August variability where scattered precipitation often trims extremes by 1–2°C. Recent model consensus reinforces this range, with no strong signals for rapid intensification or clearing that would push values to 33°C or higher, or conversely allow a cooler outlier below 29°C.

Market-implied probabilities reflect this tight clustering, as traders weigh the high likelihood of modest cooling from clouds and showers against the ongoing seasonal heat background. Updated JMA briefings and any late-model runs on August 4–5 will be the key near-term catalysts.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Trader sentiment for Munich’s August 6 high temperature centers on a narrow cluster around 27–29 °C because short-range models show persistent warm advection under a broad European high-pressure ridge, offset by the risk of afternoon convection.** 

As of early August 2026, the region remains under the influence of a heat-dome pattern that has already produced readings near 31 °C earlier in the week. ECMWF and DWD guidance indicate 850 hPa temperatures supportive of surface maxima in the upper 20s °C, with light westerly flow and modest boundary-layer moisture. The leading 28 °C and 29 °C-or-higher buckets (combined ~58 % market-implied probability) reflect this baseline warmth, while the sizable 27 °C share captures the moderating effect of increasing instability. 

Thundery showers noted in BBC guidance for the 6th could reduce insolation during peak heating hours or trigger localized downdrafts, shaving 1–2 °C off the daily maximum at the official station. Conversely, any delay or weakening of convection would allow stronger diurnal warming and push readings toward 29–30 °C. These small differences in convective timing, cloud cover, and exact station measurement explain why the three central outcomes remain closely matched rather than any single bucket dominating. Updated model runs through the 5th will be the next key data points for traders.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Tokyo Haneda Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/jp/tokyo/RJTT.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent Japan Meteorological Agency forecasts issued August 4 project a maximum of 33°C for Tokyo on August 6, with a minimum of 26°C under mostly cloudy conditions, aligning with the seasonal normal of 31.8°C. Trader sentiment clusters tightly around 32–33°C because numerical weather models show modest day-to-day variability from cloud cover, sea-breeze timing, and urban heat-island amplification in central Tokyo. High humidity typical of the season reduces the diurnal temperature range, while any late-day showers could cap the peak near 32°C; conversely, clearer skies or stronger subsidence would favor 33°C. Historical August maxima frequently reach these values, so the closely matched market odds reflect genuine forecast uncertainty rather than extreme departures. Updated model runs and JMA briefings over the next 48 hours remain the key catalysts likely to shift probabilities.
